newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares hit tenth record high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares hit tenth record high.

text.p: Egyptian share prices hit its tenth record high in a row on Thursday amid brisk trade, boosted by dealings in United Arab Spinning and Weaving/Unirab.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 2.29 points from Wednesday to close at 372.18 points on turnover of 87.79 million pounds ($25.82 million)
The partially privatised Unirab was the most active share, with shares worth 46.31 million pounds changing hands. But it ended 3.98 pounds down to 79.01.
The government has announced the sale of a minimum of ten percent of the firm, or 570,400 shares, earlier this month. The offer has already closed.
The housing and cement sectors were still dominating the trade.

Medinet Nasr and Development, one of the market's favourites, came third on the top ten list in terms of turnover. Shares worth some 4.93 million pounds were traded, but the share closed unchanged at 471.00.
Helwan Portland Cement rose 1.70 pounds to 82.50. Amriyah Cement also rose 0.66 pounds to 85.00.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 603.3 from 604.02 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 249.99 from 245.67.
Out of the 77 shares traded, 43 gained, 17 lost and 17 ended the day unchanged.
